text: Those who are strong in a subject may take it at a more demanding level, while those who find it difficult to cope with a subject may offer it at a less demanding level, based on their school’s guidance.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will also shift away from course-based subject offerings under Full SBB.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, students currently in Express and Normal (Academic) courses who face exceptional difficulties with Mother Tongue Language (MTL) learning may take MTL "B".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MOE will provide more details later in the year on other curriculum changes that accompany Full SBB.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To allow more students to benefit, MOE will extend Full SBB to more schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: From 2024, they will go on board Full SBB and admit a wider range of students, including students taking mainly G2 subjects.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Students of more diverse learning profiles can then benefit from these schools’ distinctive programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Full SBB represents a major shift to customise learning to each student according to their strengths.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: However, I must say, Full SBB does require more resources.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It entails more complex coordination of timetables and requires our teachers to adapt their teaching methods for a wider range of students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Customisation also means giving schools the flexibility to best support their students' needs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim spoke on later school start times.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In MOE, we have a simple baseline – schools are not to start before 7.30 am.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Beyond that, schools decide when to start and end, based on factors like their unique needs, student profiles and the local transport situation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, Junyuan Secondary School starts at 8.30 am twice a week and 8.00 am the other three days, and Junyuan Secondary is not the only school that has different start times.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will also adjust post-secondary admissions, to better recognise students’ individual strengths.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will continue to review admissions for other pathways to better recognise the different subject levels under Full SBB.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Next, we will expand Direct School Admission (DSA) for Government and Government-aided Junior Colleges (JCs).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This recognises other forms of merit beyond academic grades.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our efforts to customise education continue after Secondary school.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Last year, Second Minister for Education Dr Maliki Osman led the Review of Opportunities and Pathways in Applied Education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The review aims to enhance Polytechnic and ITE education to support our students’ diverse strengths and aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Its recommendations include providing students with greater flexibility in their pathways and supporting them in navigating these pathways, enhancing their career readiness and resilience for the future economy and equipping them with life skills and expanding opportunities for deeper industry exposure.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Second Minister for Education will update more later.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must also help our students to be curious about the world.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Around two-thirds of our schools have established partnerships with their overseas counterparts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Building on this, we want every school to have an overseas partnership.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This facilitates more student exchanges, so that students can broaden their horizons and learn about different cultures.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: While the exchanges have been virtual for now, because of COVID-19, technology allows our students and their overseas peers to still learn, play and celebrate special occasions together.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Chair, we will give our students greater confidence to venture beyond Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will pilot a modular Third Language programme so that more Secondary school students can learn new languages and discover other cultures.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Starting with one or two of our existing Third Language offerings, students can pick up the language from different starting points or at different levels and build their proficiency and "stack" modules towards a certificate.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: At the same time, our students must have a sense of rootedness and identity.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As Dr Wan Rizal said, our bilingual ability helps us to navigate across cultures.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Every student should learn their Mother Tongue to as high a level as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Hence, we have a range of Mother Tongue Language special programmes, like the Language Elective Programme (LEP), which we have expanded to our secondary schools in 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It allows those strong in their Mother Tongue to learn it at a higher level and nurture their interest in literature and culture.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Elective Programme in Malay Language for Secondary Schools (EMAS) is another example.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Students with a strong proficiency in the Malay language can develop their interest for the Malay language and culture.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Across the system, we continue to pay special attention to students with greater needs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They too must have the opportunities and resilience to overcome challenges and do well in life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our philosophy is this: no student should be held back from their dreams and aspirations because of his or her starting circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, we will press on with UPLIFT in schools, ITE and the Polytechnics to support students with Special Educational Needs and to support the mental well-being of our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Chair, this is our social compact – to continually invest in our people, enable every Singaporean to develop to their fullest potential regardless of their starting point and to partake in the country's growth so that we can strive towards a fairer and more inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Previously, we have focused on investing in the first 20 to 25 years of our people's lives.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: On average, we spend a quarter of a million dollars on each child to prepare him or her for their first job.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But now, firms and workers face greater disruption and faster skills obsolescence.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: On the other hand, beyond paper qualifications, those with the relevant skills, who can take advantage of the new technologies, will benefit the most.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Therefore, we will need to seriously intensify efforts on continual learning throughout life, as Mr Yip Hon Weng and Ms Mariam Jaafar mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will be the next needle-mover for the competitiveness of our people beyond their first work-ready qualification.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will become a key pillar of our social compact with Singaporeans we will invest in every Singaporean not just in school but throughout life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are focusing on two areas: providing more opportunities for our people to pursue a degree or diploma, especially as working adults, and enhancing structural support for mid-career reskilling.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Today, we have a 40% cohort participation rate target for subsidised university places for fresh school leavers and an additional 10% allowance for adult learners.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As we increasingly move towards interspersing working and learning throughout life, we should look beyond the proportion of each cohort that goes to university before starting work.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We should focus instead on ensuring that Singaporeans can upskill continually according to their needs and aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This ties in with major efforts to transform our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The refresh of the Industry Transformation Maps (ITM) aims to create more good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: With more and better job opportunities for degree holders, we will study increasing the "lifetime cohort participation rate".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will provide more opportunities for working adults to pursue a degree at a suitable point in their life and support key growth areas in our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MOE, together with MTI and MOM, will further study the mix of the increase in places to better cater to the needs of our learners and the economy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Beyond expanding degree places, we need other ways to strengthen support for our mid-career workers, especially those in their forties and fifties.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They are more vulnerable to retrenchment and long-term unemployment and need greater support to pivot to new job roles.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This structural change is here to stay post-pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will be a permanent feature of our training and placement ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The SCTP will support the career transition needs of Singaporeans, with industry-relevant training involving potential employers, and employment facilitation into sectors with good hiring opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Minister of State Gan Siow Huang will elaborate later.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Beyond these moves, MOE, MTI, MOM and MOF are studying how we can enhance the structural support for Singaporeans in their mid-forties and fifties who may need significant reskilling to provide a second wind to their careers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Regardless if our workers are looking to switch industries or jobs, they recognise that their current jobs need upgraded skills to keep pace with evolving business models and technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Reskilling can help them to keep up with the changes and remain employable.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will take a holistic review of the accessibility and the different support that adult learners need, to help every Singaporean enhance their career resilience by refreshing their skills throughout life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Chair, we need to strengthen and transform our higher education and training ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Rather than simply ramping up quantity, we must also enhance quality and accessibility.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must accelerate the transformation of our training to better cater to adult learners, leveraging on technology to enable every individual to learn at their own pace, anytime and anywhere.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will improve how we reach out to individuals and support their upskilling as they pursue their career goals through new partnerships with companies, trade associations and chambers and of course, our unions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: All three pillars of our ecosystem, our institutes for continual learning, private training providers and employers, all must pull together in the same direction.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, our Institutes of Higher Learning must grow into institutes for continual learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To cater to more diverse learners, our institutions need to review their programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Adults' learning needs, commitments and prior experiences differ from our younger learners.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This means improving andragogy, or adult education by using technology to make learning accessible and achievable and making learning bite-sized and on-the-go based on their existing skills foundation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For instance, SUSS's flexible, modular and applied curriculum, accompanied by online provisions, caters well to adult learners.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The curriculum is taught by a mix of SUSS full-time and associate faculty, many of whom are industry practitioners.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is supported by learning analytics to tailor learning to individual students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: New pathways are also being created, like SIT's new Competency-based Workplace Learning Pathway.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Skills and competencies acquired through prior work experience also count towards the graduating requirements.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: All our institutions also offer stackable pathways for learners to take bite-sized modules that count towards a full qualification.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This gives our adult learners more flexibility to juggle work, study and family responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Second, we need a stronger nexus between our institutions and industry, as Ms Mariam Jaafar suggested.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our institutions need to do so in three ways.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, partnering industry to provide more workplace learning opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Two, ensuring that our institutions' faculty remain industry relevant.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must encourage faculty to gain industry-relevant knowledge and competencies and most importantly, to keep them current.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our institutions will ramp up industry engagement and attachment opportunities and hire faculty with industry experience to complement existing faculty.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Three, collaborating with industry on research and innovation projects.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will provide additional support to our Centres engaging in Technology, Innovation and Enterprise activities in our Polytechnics and ITE.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They can then partner more SMEs on innovation projects and that will allow our SMEs and companies to be a ready receptacle for our upgraded workers and upgraded students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our companies also need to take ownership of this transformation because transforming themselves to attract, retain and upskill local talent is an important piece of this jigsaw puzzle.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Over the past year, MOE, MTI, and MOM initiated efforts with industry leaders, unions and other Government agencies, and educators to strengthen the employability and career prospects of our Polytechnic and ITE graduates in the future economy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We looked into raising the quantity and quality of internships and on-the-job upskilling opportunities for our students, starting with sectors like Manufacturing, Built environment, Information and Communications Technology (ICT), Retail and Food Services.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have developed strategies to promote access to jobs with good career prospects.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have encouraged companies to recognise the skills and competencies of our Polytechnic and ITE graduates and invest in talent attraction and retention and also to invest in their workers' continued education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Good internship experiences and progression pathways are key to encouraging our students to join and stay in the sector they were trained for.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Chair, MOE cannot transform our education system by ourselves.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We need and want to partner educators, parents, industry and our community to achieve this vision.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Darryl David, Dr Wan Rizal and Mr Louis Ng have spoken about them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To inspire our students, we need to inspire our teachers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To widen the exposure for our students, we need to widen the exposure for our teachers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To empower our teachers to steward change, we will partner with the people, public and private sectors so that teachers can take up more short-term attachments.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our teachers must then be able to grow and they must grow as they help our children grow.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Many Polytechnic and ITE educators have prior working experiences from our industry.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: However, we also need to help them keep pace amidst the current fast changes in the industry.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will therefore send more Polytechnic and ITE educators for industry attachments and for more of them to have collaboration projects with our companies, including many SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will refresh their skill sets and keep their competencies at the frontier.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our educators have worked much harder and for much longer hours in the last two years.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In MOE, we have a saying, "One cannot pour from an empty cup." Hence, we will continue to take care of our teachers' mental well-being and workload.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Schools are committed to ensuring that workload remains manageable and we will continue to work towards all schools having Wellness Ambassadors.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To strengthen the culture of care and peer support for our teachers, Staff Well-Being Committees will place more emphasis on the mental well-being of our teachers, with support from MOE headquarters.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These efforts complement free in-house counselling services at iCARE and the free 24/7 whole-of-Government counselling hotline.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked about teachers’ appraisal.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our teachers are driven by a strong sense of mission and responsibility for our students, and it shows in their work and attitude.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Therefore, it is important for us to recognise and affirm deserving teachers, especially those who have gone beyond their call of duty, those who have excelled, and those who have set the pace for the fraternity.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: At the same time, we need to identify teachers who require more support, so that we can build and sustain an excellent workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Louis Ng can be assured that we are constantly updating our policies so that all our teachers can continue to have access to our training programmes and be guided to improve, to better nurture our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We also hear Mr Edward Chia’s call to support instructors and coaches.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our second group of partners are our parents.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Let us help our children acquire skills based on their interests and strengths that will allow them to have a unique value proposition when they join the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This strengthens their value proposition, our collective diversity and resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Let us work together to support the well-being and development of our children – not to chase after the marginal last mark, instil fear of failure, or excessively compare our children’s achievements with others.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Let us help them surpass themselves throughout life, rather than just surpass others in an examination.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MOE will continue to partner and support our parents.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will provide parenting resources and tips throughout our platforms and work closely with Parent Support Groups.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our partners, like the council members from COMmunity and PArents in Support of Schools (COMPASS), have also initiated ground-up efforts to support parents.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As I have stressed earlier, industry needs to work closely with our institutes for continual learning, provide learning opportunities for our students to prepare them for the workforce and transform themselves to create good jobs for our graduates.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Companies which partner our institutions well will also have the first call to the next generation of talent, and this is a significant competitive advantage.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: All of us can contribute to this effort as well.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, as school alumni, we can give back to our alma mater, by mentoring younger students and giving them career advice.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Let us all acknowledge the support we received from the community and the opportunities we received from society.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Therefore, it is also our responsibility to give back where we can, so others may benefit as we have, so that every generation of Singaporeans can aspire to do better than the previous generation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Only so will we continue to preserve education as an uplifting force for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Chairman, may I have your permission for my MOE colleagues to elaborate on the various MOE policies please.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, every child is important to us.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MOE is committed to supporting our students to achieve their fullest potential, regardless of their background.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We agree with Mr Shawn Huang and Mr Leon Perera on the importance of supporting students in disadvantaged circumstances.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These students may not have the best environment or opportunities to support their learning.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some may face challenges at home that could translate into poor attendance, motivation and self-esteem.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are committed to ensuring that these students are not limited by their starting points in life.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Across the system, we have dedicated programmes and support based on the students’ areas of need, including academic and socio-emotional support, financial assistance and provisions for special education needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our teachers pay extra attention to them, tirelessly reaching out to their parents, making home visits to understand their circumstances and providing support when the children are in school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But our teachers do so with passion and commitment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Introduced in 2018, UPLIFT has been actively helping students from disadvantaged backgrounds achieve success.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Hafiza’s mother is the sole breadwinner of the family, which includes her and her infant stepbrother.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Hafiza’s mother was busy with work and rarely around to guide Hafiza when she was growing up.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Hafiza felt lost and unmotivated and ended up mixing with bad company.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: She ran away from home several times, missed school frequently and felt disengaged from her teachers and peers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Hafiza was touched by their concern and, gradually, opened up to them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Hafiza's teachers encouraged her to join after-school activities, like the Youth Community Outreach Patrol, where she built positive relationships with her peers and mentors who helped her gain confidence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The UPLIFT Town-Level Coordinator and a volunteer family befriender also worked with the Family Service Centre and other agencies to provide the financial and emotional support the family needed and find ways to provide a more conducive home environment for Hafiza.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, Hafiza’s mother made alternative care arrangements for Hafiza's infant brother, to allow Hafiza to focus on her studies for her graduating year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through these efforts, Hafiza achieved good results at the GCE "N" Level examination last year and progressed to a course of her choice in ITE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: When I met Hafiza, I could see the confidence in her eyes and was proud to see a young girl turn around and do better with self-determination and support from the community around her.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Hafiza’s example illustrates three key components of support we will provide our students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we will provide a supportive school environment responsive to the needs of each student.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Providing customised support and attention to students with higher needs requires time and dedication.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, we will keep students meaningfully engaged in programmes after school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many of these students do not have conducive home environments and many of us know about it.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through a structured and nurturing after-school environment, we give them the opportunity to develop routines and skills to succeed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Since 2020, MOE has set up a Student Care Centre in every Primary school to provide a safe environment for students to rest, play, do their homework and engage in meaningful after-school activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With subsidies under the ComCare Student Care Fee Assistance scheme, eligible students pay as little as $5 per month.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also reaching out to help parents who have concerns over enrolling their child, like providing the necessary supporting documents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last year, teachers in our Primary schools helped more than 700 students from disadvantaged families enrol in our Student Care Centres.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are seeing good progress made by these students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many are more confident, they are more engaged in school and also more engaged in after-school activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to help more disadvantaged families enrol their children into our Student Care Centres.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our focus on after-school programmes continues into the Secondary school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: About 120 Secondary schools provide after-school mentoring and motivational support under the GEAR-UP programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Third, we are building a strong network of community partners to complement efforts in schools and address challenges that the families of these students face.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We started the UPLIFT Community pilot in 2020, creating a network of agencies, including Family Service Centres, Social Service Agencies and relevant Government agencies like ECDA and HDB.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The pilot has supported more than 300 students in four towns so far.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Most have seen improved attendance and their families have seen increased community support for them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Encouraged by the success, we will expand this pilot.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The UPLIFT Community Network has been rolled out to eight new towns in 2022.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are grateful to our community partners who have been supporting our UPLIFT efforts and I urge more members of the community to step forward.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition to support for each student, we are also expanding pathways and opportunities across the educational system to cater to the different aspirations and needs of our students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I will now elaborate on our efforts in our applied education.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While we will provide equal access to opportunities to all our children, it is natural for each generation of parents who are better off to be able give their children a head-start in life, sometimes leading to unequal outcomes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The link between socio-economic background and student outcomes that Mr Leon Perera has observed and is concerned with is not unique to Singapore and, in fact, is seen across countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is part of societal progress and development which result in social mobility for most, albeit at a different pace.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There will always be those who are slower due to challenging circumstances.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: What is important is that we give them the best support we can to develop the best that they can, enable them to move up the social and economic ladder, and do better than their parents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As I have told the House earlier, we are encouraged by our students from less advantaged backgrounds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They do well, compared to their international counterparts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This gives us confidence and conviction to press on with our efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Beyond targeted support and programmes like UPLIFT, we want to help all our students to be confident and resilient in the face of adversity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As part of adolescent development, our youths face pressures on multiple fronts – from themselves, parents, peers, or from society.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This challenge is made more complex because technology has transformed the way our young people live today.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Despite its benefits, technology and social media use can also distort their self-image and increase social pressure for many of our youths.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Improving youth mental well-being requires a coordinated effort.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Minister Chan Chun Sing described earlier how we will give students more opportunities to develop holistically in school, and Minister of State Sun Xueling will share how we can equip parents to support their child’s well-being.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we equip students with the social-emotional skills to be resilient.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We want our students to be confident in themselves, to acknowledge their limitations and celebrate their strengths.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, one lesson teaches students how people respond to challenges quite differently.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Students discover their signs of distress when they reach their limits of coping.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They are encouraged to look out to others for support and realise that these experiences are normal.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At different points in time in their lives, given the circumstances and experiences, they need help and it is normal for them to seek help.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, we are strengthening the supportive relationships around students, so no student feels that they face their challenges alone.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is especially important, as Dr Wan Rizal says, there are those who are suffering in silence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The more they are connected with friends, we hope the more ready they are to come out early, should they face some challenges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Youths often seek out their peers for a listening ear.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, every school has a peer support system that empowers students to look out for one another and build strong social support networks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Activities such as CCAs and camps also help students develop strong connections with their peers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Students also look to their teachers for support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Teachers use CCE periods and form teacher periods to offer pastoral care.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Schools have also set aside dedicated time and space at the start of each term for teachers to engage students on their well-being, be it managing relationship stress or other academic stresses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Third, we provide students with access to the care that they need.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They actively look out for signs of distress, offer support and refer students to counselling resources in school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our efforts to strengthen the confidence and resilience of our students extend to our Institutes of Higher Learning, or IHLs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Polytechnics and ITE offer a mental wellness curriculum to all students to provide a better understanding of mental health issues and where to seek help.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They are also equipping more students with skills to support their peers as peer supporters.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will strengthen professional development, so that these tutors can provide better care for their students and study ways to enhance their contact time with their students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Another area we are studying is the coordination of care and support for students with more complex needs in the Polytechnics and ITE, as it often includes working with external stakeholders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Autonomous Universities have also introduced mental wellness programmes, including online modules and training workshops to equip students to help look after their mental and emotional well-being.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They also have in-house counsellors available for our students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, let me now talk about enhancements to our Polytechnics and ITE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We agree with Mr Sharael Taha, Mr Abdul Samad and Mr Shawn Huang on the need to prepare students for the jobs of tomorrow, especially given the pace of industry transformation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: IHLs regularly review their course offerings and curriculum in collaboration with industry and economic agencies, to keep pace with the latest developments and ensure our students secure good jobs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our Polytechnics and ITE are a key part of our higher education landscape, catering to seven in 10 of each Primary school cohort.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As we prepare our students for the future economy and their future, we also acknowledge the growing diversity in interests and aspirations amongst our young people.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This was an area studied by the Review of Opportunities and Pathways in Applied Education launched last year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we agree with Dr Wan Rizal on the importance of providing flexible pathways for students to discover and pursue their interests.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This gives students ownership of their learning and a more fulfilling educational journey that helps them find meaningful careers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have expanded admissions to allow students to enter the Polytechnics and ITE based on interests and aptitude, more than just their academic performance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The expanded range of Common Entry Programmes in the Polytechnics also allows students more room to explore their interests before specialising.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, we will continue to equip students with deeper industry ready skills.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This was consistent feedback that we receive from both students, industries and other stakeholders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Indeed, rather than just learning in a classroom, we want our students to learn from active practitioners and be inspired by the range of opportunities out there.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will pilot the provision of earlier industry exposure opportunities for students in the Polytechnics from AY2022, beyond their final-year internships.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We agree with Dr Shahira Abdullah on the importance of securing good outcomes for our ITE graduates.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This was why we introduced the enhanced three-year ITE curricular structure last year, to meet the aspirations of our ITE graduates to deepen their skills and upgrade beyond a Nitec qualification.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am confident that these students will be well-supported and able to make full use of the opportunities in ITE to discover and pursue their interests.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ITE will review the outcomes from this first phase of implementation and move more courses into the enhanced curricular structure after AY 2024.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As more ITE graduates obtain the Higher Nitec qualification, we will provide them options to deepen their skills and meet their aspirations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Results for the Class of 2021 will be ready later this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Besides our Polytechnic Diplomas, ITE’s Technical Diplomas, or TDs, and Work-Study Diplomas, or WSDips, provide an alternative form of learning with a greater emphasis on learning-by-doing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I met Sharon, for example, a graduate from ITE’s Higher Nitec in Cyber and Network Security.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Upon graduation, Sharon pursued her interest in F&B initially.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, she discovered that she still had a strong passion for IT, and wanted to deepen her knowledge and skills.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Sharon was informed about the Work-Study Diploma programme in Cyber Security and Forensics by her ITE lecturer and decided to take it up.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This allowed her to embark on a career in a cybersecurity firm, in a sector that is increasingly important.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Among the batch of graduates in 2021, around 80% stayed on with their host companies after graduation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These students saw an average increase in salary of about 20% upon completion of their diploma, with many taking on higher-level job roles.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Students can look forward to more opportunities as ITE works with industry partners and other educational institutions to expand their diploma programmes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have made progress in our plans to provide 1,000 WSDip places per year in 2025.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In 2022, ITE will offer 36 WSDip programmes, catering to over 500 students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ITE also offers three Technical Diplomas, or TDs, in Automotive Engineering, Machine Technology and Culinary Arts, catering to around 100 students per intake.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They plan to expand their TD offerings to other engineering, business and service domains.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Through these enhancements, we will continue to support the diverse needs and aspirations of our students, and prepare our graduates to learn for life and succeed in a wide range of fields.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to say a few words in Malay.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: (In Malay):   Chairman, the learning of Mother Tongue languages is an important part of our vision to help our students remain rooted and appreciate their culture.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: During the Budget debates, Mr Faisal Manap shared his concerns about how our children would develop strong Malay language skills.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: This is something that we should be proud of although we acknowledge the challenges that they face due to exposure to the use of English language in today's world.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: At the policy level in MOE, we are pressing ahead with important reforms to our education system.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We need to be prepared for a future where technological and business cycles are more compressed and the demand for skills is more dynamic, and also a future where our world is increasingly polarized and fragmented, even as we remain more interconnected and interdependent.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: A future where our social fabric continues to evolve as well, with more diverse aspirations and perspectives amongst our people.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Our vision for the education system has three key elements.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: First, we want all Singaporeans to have confidence in our abilities and ourselves, so we can keep growing and maximise our full potential.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Second, we want all Singaporeans to continue to maintain our competitive advantage, through the ability to learn and re-learn, and our connectivity with the world.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Third, for us continue to appreciate and celebrate diversity, even as we work to forge a shared identity, Achieving this vision requires us to rethink our approach to education.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Our education is no longer something which ends in schools, but a continuous journey throughout our lives.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: At a young age, we will build strong foundations for all students and spark their curiosity and desire for learning.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: In schools, we will continue to free up time and space for students to discover their strengths and cultivate future-ready competencies.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: In higher education, we will continue to equip our students with the skills and competencies to succeed as they transit to the workforce.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: At the same time, our Institutes of Higher Learning will also grow into their roles as institutes for continual learning, working closely with industry to enhance the quality and accessibility of their upskilling and reskilling programmes for adult learners.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Chairman, we will continue to enhance our education system for the future of our children and our country.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We need the support of all Singaporeans in this effort.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Educators, parents, as well as community and industry partners all play a key role in developing a future that enable Singaporeans to have the confidence to chart their own path, and the resilience to respond to changes and disruptions.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: (In English): As we embark on the enhancements to our education system, we will help our students to make the best of these changes.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Together, we will nurture generations of confident and resilient students who are prepared to face the challenges and opportunities of the future economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Chan Chun Sing has emphasised that we need to adopt a lifetime view towards learning instead of relying only on the education that we go through in the first 20 years or so of our lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our higher education institutions and adult training system must provide re-tooling opportunities for Singaporeans as they journey through different jobs over their career lifetimes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is important that we do this well as it enables Singaporeans to remain employable and access good jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is why MOE has worked closely with our Statutory Board SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) to push ahead with our efforts to strengthen our Continuing Education and Training (CET) ecosystem, as Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Shawn Huang and Mr Darryl David have asked about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Under SkillsFuture, we have been expanding the range of opportunities for Singaporeans to regularly reskill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is especially important for mid-career workers who need to re-tool in the face of fast-changing technologies and new trends.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The need for reskilling was particularly evident during the pandemic, which brought great disruption to our industries and workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To address this, we introduced the Enhanced Training Support Package that helped enterprises make productive use of the downtime to train their workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As part of the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package, we launched the SGUnited Skills (SGUS) and SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways – Company Training (SGUP-CT) programmes to help mid-career individuals acquire new skills and capture new career opportunities as the economy recovers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We worked with 18 CET Centres and 16 companies to provide industry-relevant training, coupled with employment facilitation, to help jobseekers secure placements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For SGUP-CT with companies, such as Google and IBM, more than half the trainees found jobs as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I met Mr Oscar Yong last year, one of our SGUS graduates who successfully switched to a new career in food manufacturing after working for more than 20 years in the electronics sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: He was displaced from his previous job when his company relocated overseas in 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: He signed up for the six-month SGUS Advanced Manufacturing Programme at the Singapore Institute of Management in the hopes of making a career switch.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As part of the programme, Oscar did an industry attachment with Super Bean International.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: He performed well during the attachment and was offered a job of assistant manager of inventory and quality control when he graduated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I am heartened by Oscar's determination to reskill in pursuit of a new career and I hope that his story will inspire more Singaporeans to upskill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The SCTP will be our steady-state train-and-place programme for mid-career individuals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It will be delivered by IHLs and selected private training providers and will incorporate key features of the SGUS and SGUP-CT which have worked well to strengthen training outcomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: First, skills and training advisory services will be made available upfront to help trainees select courses that best suit their strengths and interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Second, all courses will have elements of industry involvement, such as industry projects or attachments with companies, to enable trainees to acquire industry-relevant skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Third, employment facilitation and career coaching will be part of the SCTP to support trainees in their job search.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: SCTP will have a duration of between three and 12 months and we plan to launch them in sectors with good hiring opportunities, such as ICT and advanced manufacturing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: On top of this, to ensure that jobseekers with greater needs can access the SCTP, we will provide additional subsidies to cover up to 95% of course fees for eligible Singapore Citizens who are lower-income earners, long-term unemployed or persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The SCTP is part of the continuum of initiatives by SSG and Workforce Singapore (WSG) to ramp up reskilling opportunities for Singaporeans who are looking for jobs or considering career switches.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: By working closely together to offer a suite of place-and-train, attach-and-train and train-and-place programmes and by jointly delivering outreach at career fairs and SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centres in the heartlands, SSG and WSG are aligned in their efforts to help Singaporeans access good jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: When we started to scale up the provision of career transition programmes at the CET Centres in 2020, we also provided additional SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career Support) to enable Singaporeans in their 40s and 50s to access such programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Along the way, we received feedback about individuals who may not intend to switch careers but would, nevertheless, like to utilise their credit to pursue meaningful upskilling to remain employable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To this end, I am glad to share that we will expand the range of courses that the additional SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career Support) can be used for.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The list will remain focused on courses that deliver good employment outcomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: These include SkillsFuture Series courses in IHLs, industry-relevant courses offered by CET Centres, including private training providers, and courses which enable workers to progress in sectors with the Progressive Wage Model.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: While we strengthen support for individual upskilling, I agree with Ms Foo Mee Har that enterprises also have an integral role to play in supporting their employees in their skills development journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We also agree on the importance of workplace learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is why we have incorporated elements of workplace learning into many of our CET offerings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For example, the SkillsFuture Work-Study Programmes allow trainees to upskill through a combination of structured on-the-job training and classroom learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To increase such opportunities, we rely on employers to step up to deliver quality trailing at the workplace and we will continue to support them in their endeavour to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have expanded the reach of the National Centre of Excellence for Workplace Learning (NACE) to uplift the workplace learning capabilities of companies, especially SMEs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We also encourage enterprises to play the role of SkillsFuture Queen Bees to mobilise other companies within their networks to engage in training and upskilling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This will raise the capabilities of the sector as a whole and enhance their competitive advantage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: SSG has been expanding partnerships with enterprises through the SkillsFuture Queen Bee initiative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Sheng Siong is an example of a company which took on the role of a SkillsFuture Queen Bee and is helping its suppliers build up workforce capabilities to accelerate the adoption of digital technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: With the support of Skills Managers and training providers, Sheng Siong has reached out to more than 60 suppliers to customise skills development interventions based on their business needs and skills gaps.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This includes SkillsFuture for Digital Workplace courses to build foundational digital skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Sheng Siong is also integrating SkillsFuture courses and resources into their supplier portal to encourage their wider network of suppliers to engage in continuous learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Such examples show us the significance and impact of enterprises taking on a more proactive role in supporting skills development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is why we have pressed on with our plans under the next bound of SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Strengthening the role of enterprises in driving workforce transformation will continue to be our key priority in the coming years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As we ramp up our efforts to drive enterprise-led training, we can tap on unions and industry intermediaries as our key partners, too.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: With their extensive networks and understanding of companies’ needs on the ground, they can help us broaden outreach, aggregate skills demand and spread the benefits of our job-skills interventions to more companies and workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our tripartite partners are supporting companies in their business and workforce transformation efforts, such as through NTUC's Company Training Committees (CTCs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Employers are supported in their firm-level action plans in areas like employment facilitation, job redesign and training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: SSG can complement the CTC process by helping these companies build their skills development capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: SSG’s partnership with PM Link and the Building Construction and Timber Industries Employees’ Union, which formed a CTC in 2019, is an illustration of how this can be done.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Over the past two years, SSG worked with the CTC to pilot a skills profiling digital solution that is based on SSG’s Skills Frameworks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: PM Link, a project management company in the building and construction industry, used the Skills Frameworks to identify core competencies for their workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This enabled their employees to self-assess and benchmark their skills proficiencies against industry standards, identify relevant training to address skills gaps and participate in SSG-supported courses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We also want to better tap on industry intermediaries, such as trade associations and chambers (TACs) and professional bodies, as they have deep industry networks and great agility in sensing the jobs-skills needs of employers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This will help companies better plan for workforce upgrading and improve job mobility of individual workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: SSG is also exploring similar partnerships with other TACs to expand outreach to more sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to conclude in Mandarin please.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: (In Mandarin):   Building a strong skills ecosystem is essential to ensure that our workforce can access quality training opportunities throughout their lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We endeavour to build a robust ecosystem that leverages the different strengths of the IHLs, private training providers, NTUC, TACs and industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, as we work towards our vision of Confident Singaporeans, a Competitive Singapore and a Cohesive Society, we remain committed to supporting students with different needs, to enable them to develop confidence in their future and the skills and resilience to do well in life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOE has developed our landscape of support significantly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to enhance support for students with SEN throughout their educational journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I agree with Mr Gerald Giam that some children with SEN need more intensive interventions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will say more about the early intervention provided for preschoolers at MSF’s COS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In our mainstream schools, all students with SEN, with or without a diagnosis, can get support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As part of our whole-school approach, support is provided through inclusive classroom practices by all teachers, guided by Teachers Trained in Special Needs and Allied Educators in learning and behavioural support, or AEDs(LBS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: A small number of students may need individualised therapy delivered in clinical settings, or they may need a customised curriculum in a SPED school.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For these students, schools work with MOE Educational Psychologists and parents to facilitate referrals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOE is constantly innovating to develop evidence-based interventions for the skills development of students with SEN.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: School-based Dyslexia Remediation, Circle of Friends and Facing Your Fears are examples.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Entering Primary 1 can be a major transition point for our students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some students may need additional support in developing social and behavioural skills to cope with this transition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Last year, I shared that MOE was implementing TRANSIT for P1 students with social and behavioural needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With TRANSIT, students receive support from Allied Educators in learning and behaviour support and teachers at P1 to learn and apply self-management skills, to get ready to learn independently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I visited North Vista Primary recently and saw how students in TRANSIT had dedicated teaching resources to support them in their management of their socio-emotional needs, as well as in their abilities to interact with others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We had announced in 2019 that we are working with our SSAs to set up three new Government-funded SPED schools that can support students with Autism Spectrum Disorder who can access the national curriculum, but need to learn in a SPED setting due to their moderate level of SEN.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: One of these schools is St Andrew’s Mission School (SAMS), which began operating in January 2022 at Bukit Batok.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These students have complex needs which can affect their learning and mobility and may also face medical challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Families can look forward to strong support for their child’s holistic development with SPED educators, Allied Professionals and parents working closely together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We wholeheartedly agree with Ms Denise Phua that our vision to develop the full potential of our students with SEN should be a shared vision, requiring close partnerships with key stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOE works closely with schools, Early Intervention Centres, the Department of Child Development in hospitals, sister agencies and organisations, such as ECDA and SG Enable as well as, very importantly, our SSAs, to meet families’ needs at different stages of their journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We thank Ms Phua for her vision of the impact that SPED schools should have.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We believe in the SPED schools and in our SSAs which run them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are committed to resourcing them well, financially and through co-developing quality SPED curriculum and investing in SPED teaching.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The development of the SPED sector is situated within the larger Enabling Masterplan 2030.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOE is committed to co-creating solutions in the range of areas beyond SPED, across the lifespan of the children and families that we serve.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Both within and beyond special needs, MOE has been strengthening our partnerships with parents to equip our children so that they have the resourcefulness, resilience and confidence to meet challenges in the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Phua and Ms Carrie Tan have brought across the critical role of parents, as what happens at home complements what happens in schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will support parents in the following ways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, we will strengthen our partnerships with parents through the COMmunity and Parents in Support of Schools (COMPASS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is a different COMPASS from MOM's Complementarity Assessment framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOE's COMPASS council has embarked on efforts to support parents as we continue to encourage broader definitions of success.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, COMPASS has organised a series of Facebook Live sessions to create awareness of different pathways of excellence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The first session was held with industry leaders to discuss the qualities that make for a future-ready individual and the need to broaden definitions of success for our children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The next two sessions will share perspectives from parents and individuals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They are partnering the Singapore Kindness Movement to provide resources to raise parents’ awareness and understanding of cyber wellness and kindness and how they can support their children in it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, MOE is working closely with PSGs so that they can connect with and support fellow parent communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I recently met with the 25 PSGs who are leading the charge in their own ways to support parents, through understanding the parents’ needs and being creative and resourceful in meeting those needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: By providing a listening ear and being a befriender, the PSG builds a strong circle of support for parents and provides different avenues for them to reach out and seek help, such as through level group chats and parent engagement sessions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The PSG has been tapping on their student alumni to share their education and career journeys with their student and parent communities and provide tips on coping with stressors that students may face.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Parents could hear from alumni about their aspirations and struggles, which helped them to better support their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOE has launched a Mental Well-being Resource Guide and an online repository of resources for PSGs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Developed based on suggestions and feedback from PSGs, the Guide provides tips and resources that can inform PSGs’ efforts to support parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The online repository is a live document and we will work with PSGs to enhance its content over time to cover other issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Lastly, we share useful resources and tips with parents via MOE’s social media platforms and the Parents Gateway, which has a new feature called "Parenting Resources", to guide them in supporting their children’s education journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also working with partner agencies to incorporate more resources into the portal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our partnerships with parents, via COMPASS and PSGs, extend MOE’s efforts to build students’ confidence and resilience beyond the school environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also stepping up partnerships with other stakeholders in society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is particularly pertinent in the area of mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked how students with mental well-being concerns can be provided with stronger, coordinated care and support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second Minister Dr Mohamad Maliki had spoken about our strengthened support for students’ mental well-being in schools through the refreshed Character and Citizenship Education curriculum.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We recognise that the issues that affect student mental well-being are multi-faceted and stressors outside of school can have an impact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As part of this task force, MOE and MSF are working together to provide greater support for families, children and youths to enhance mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Parenting is one key area we are looking into.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I had earlier described MOE’s recent efforts, through the PSGs, to support fellow parents in taking care of their own children’s mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Through this task force, we will engage and empower a wider segment of parents with evidence-based, bite-sized parenting strategies and mental health and well-being knowledge, so that parents can build stronger relationships at home and help their child effectively meet life’s challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also explore effective ways to parent in the digital age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Another area that we are concerned about is the potential impact of the digital world on students’ mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
